name: Massachusetts
headline_status: Recreational and medical cannabis are legal for adults 21+, and voters kept legal sales in November 2026.
summary: Massachusetts allows adults 21 and older to possess, grow and buy cannabis from licensed stores, and runs a separate medical program dating to 2012. A 2026 law signed in April doubled the public possession limit to two ounces and restructured the Cannabis Control Commission. On November 3, 2026, voters rejected Question 8, which would have ended adult-use sales and home growing, by roughly three to one.

adult_use_since.value: Legalized by voters via Question 4 in November 2016; took effect December 15, 2016.

possession_limit.value: Up to 2 ounces in public (raised from 1 ounce effective April 19, 2026); up to 10 ounces inside a primary residence plus whatever home-grown plants produce.

home_grow.value: Up to 6 plants per adult, with no more than 12 plants on one premises.

retail_sales.value: Licensed adult-use stores have operated since November 20, 2018, when the first two opened.

taxes.value: 10.75% state marijuana excise plus 6.25% state sales tax on retail sales; many cities and towns add a local marijuana tax.

public_use.value: Consuming cannabis in any form, including smoking, vaping or eating, is illegal in public places and on federal land; use is allowed in private residences, subject to landlord, employer and local policies.

dui.value: Impairment-based: Massachusetts has no THC per se limit, but driving under the influence of cannabis is illegal. An open container of marijuana in a car's passenger area can bring a civil fine of up to $500; keep it closed in the trunk or a locked glove box.

tourists.value: Yes. Visitors 21+ with a valid government ID can buy at adult-use stores, but must consume it in Massachusetts. Out-of-state residents cannot buy medical marijuana.

timeline.event: First two adult-use retail stores open.
Gov. Healey signs H. 5350, doubling the public possession limit to 2 ounces and overhauling the CCC.
Voters reject Question 8, which would have repealed adult-use sales and home growing (about 76% no).

faq.a: Yes. Adults 21 and older can legally possess, grow and buy cannabis, and patients can use it under the medical program.

faq.q: How much weed can you carry in Massachusetts?
faq.a: Since April 19, 2026, adults may carry up to 2 ounces in public. At home you may keep up to 10 ounces, plus the harvest from your own plants.

faq.q: Did Massachusetts vote to end legal marijuana sales?
faq.a: No. Question 8 on the November 3, 2026 ballot would have ended adult-use sales and home growing, but voters rejected it by a wide margin.

faq.q: Can you grow cannabis at home in Massachusetts?
faq.a: Yes. Each adult may grow up to 6 plants, with a cap of 12 plants per home.

faq.q: What is the tax on marijuana in Massachusetts?
faq.a: Retail purchases carry a 10.75% state excise tax and the 6.25% state sales tax, and many municipalities add a local tax on top.
